tokyo_asakusa_nadai_ramen_yoro.price_note: PARTIAL: the shop names its bowls in its own navigation but prints a price for only one of them, the vegan ramen at ¥1,400. The seasonal announcements on the front page carry three more dated prices, recorded below as seasonal. Everything else has an empty price rather than an invented one. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE FINDING HERE IS A VEGAN RAMEN ON A 1954-STYLE ASAKUSA COUNTER, AND IT IS THE CLEANEST ILLUSTRATION IN THIS DATASET OF THE TWO DIETS COMING APART. ヴィーガンらーめん at ¥1,400 is a real, permanent, priced menu item at a traditional 和風醤油 ramen shop on Denboin-dori — which is worth knowing, because a vegan in Asakusa otherwise has very little. But a vegan ramen is not a gluten-free ramen and nothing about it moves the coeliac answer: the noodles are wheat with かん水 whatever the broth is made of, and the tare on a 醤油 bowl is soy. One diet gets a whole dish; the other gets nothing, from the same bowl. ⚠ ONE BOWL IS WORTH ASKING ABOUT ON THE OTHER AXIS: 梅しおらーめん and the しお option on the 特製 use a SALT tare rather than a soy one, which removes one of the two wheat routes. The noodle is the other and it remains, so this is a distinction that matters for understanding the kitchen rather than one that opens the door. ⚠ AND THE SEASONAL BOWLS ADD RATHER THAN SUBTRACT: the 冷やし中華 comes 特製ごまだれ付き — a sesame dressing, which in Japan is built on soy — and the 坦々つけ麺 is a sesame-and-soy dip. 伝法院通り, Asakusa.

items.note: ⚠ A PERMANENT, PRICED VEGAN BOWL AT A TRADITIONAL ASAKUSA RAMEN SHOP — rare enough to be the reason this record exists, and the most expensive bowl on the board. The shop lists it in its own menu navigation alongside the standard ramen, so it is a fixture rather than a special. ⚠ AND IT IS STILL WHEAT: a vegan broth changes the animal question and not the grain one. Ramen noodles are wheat flour and かん水, and no gluten-free noodle is offered. This is the dish that shows the two axes are independent.

The house bowl, named without a price. 和風 means the broth is built on a Japanese DASHI — bonito — and 醤油 means the tare is soy. ⚠ RAMEN NOODLES ARE WHEAT with かん水 — that is true of every bowl here including the vegan one.
The soy bowl with egg; no price published. ⚠ RAMEN NOODLES ARE WHEAT with かん水 — that is true of every bowl here including the vegan one.

tokyo_kyoto_saryo_suisen_shinj.price_note: ⚠ CHECK BEFORE YOU TRAVEL: the shop’s own page carries a notice dated 2026-07-24 headed 【新宿店】臨時休業のお知らせ — 「【休業期間】2026年8月3日（月）〜 未定」. As of the date on this record the Shinjuku branch is on an INDEFINITE temporary closure that began 3 August 2026, with no reopening date given; the operator directs customers to nearby branches. The full card is recorded anyway, because it is the branch’s own published menu. Prices as printed; the footer adds メニューの内容・価格は店舗により異なる場合がございます. 茶寮翠泉 is a Kyoto matcha house (本店 in Takatsuji) and the Shinjuku shop is in the 新宿住友ビル 1F by Tochomae, 11:00-20:00 (L.O. 19:30), no reservations. ⚠ THE SOBA HERE IS UNUSUALLY HONEST AND STILL NOT SAFE. The shop makes its own 自家製生蕎麦・茶蕎麦 and its English labels its combination plate «Matcha Juwari and Juwari Combination Soba» — 十割, i.e. 100% buckwheat with no wheat cut, which is rare and worth recording. It is still no for a coeliac: 打ち粉 dusting flour is wheat, the boiling water is shared, and the そばつゆ is a soy-and-dashi sauce. The 茶そば (Kyoto soba) is green-tea soba, which conventionally IS cut with wheat. ⚠ THE WARABIMOCHI IS THE INTERESTING ONE: warabimochi is bracken or sweet-potato starch, not wheat, and it is the house signature in half a dozen forms — but the shop publishes no allergen sheet and several versions are served with 三笠 (a dorayaki-style wheat pancake) or come «with sencha», so each needs asking. ⚠ AND THE 三笠 IS A HIDDEN WHEAT ON THREE DRINK LINES: 特選宇治抹茶, 京都宇治煎茶 and 玉露茎ほうじ茶 are all sold もちもちお抹茶三笠つき — a wheat cake comes with the tea by default.

tokyo_mazesoba_shichi.price_note: Complete お品書き from the shop’s own site (まぜそば七, 渋谷区桜丘町16-10, tel 03-3780-1176; site opened 2024-07-01, operated by the 麺 大黒屋 group per its Twitter feed). ⚠ THE PRICING RULE IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE AND IT IS EASY TO MISS: all four bowls come in four noodle weights — 小 120 g, 並 170 g, 大 250 g, 特 340 g — and the shop prints 全て同一料金!! against every one, so the LARGEST SIZE COSTS THE SAME AS THE SMALLEST. Prices below are that single flat price per bowl. ⚠ MAZESOBA IS BROTHLESS WHEAT NOODLE IN A CONCENTRATED SOY TARE — the format removes the soup, not the gluten, and the shop’s own selling point is a 焼豚 that is simmered a long time in a tare and then charcoal-grilled, which is soy twice. 台湾まぜそば is by definition finished with minced pork, garlic, nira and a chilli-soy tare, and comes here with a mini rice bowl for tipping in at the end; 七郎 is a Jiro-styled bowl. No allergen statement is published, and the site’s もっと見る control could not be expanded by this fetch, so there may be items below the four recorded.

tokyo_ramen_jiro_shinjuku_kabu.price_note: PARTIAL BY NATURE OF THE SUBJECT: Ramen Jiro branches do not run their own websites, and the URL carried in this dataset is ラーメン二郎 PC店Ⅲ, a Jiro-documentation site that catalogues the branches — not the shop's own page. It is recorded as partial for that reason, not because the numbers are shaky: the site publishes the Kabukicho board in Japanese and English on two separate pages and the two agree item-for-item and yen-for-yen, which is the strongest cross-check available for a shop of this kind. Address 東京都新宿区歌舞伎町2-37-5, 11:30-02:30, closed Wednesdays (the site adds 営業する日も有り — it sometimes opens anyway). ⚠ THERE IS NOTHING HERE FOR A COELIAC AND THAT IS NOT A GAP IN THE RESEARCH, IT IS THE DISH. Jiro is a wheat-noodle form: the noodles are thick 極太 wheat with かん水, the tare is soy, and the broth is pork back-fat and bone. Every bowl on the board is wheat by construction and there is no rice, no side and no non-noodle item to fall back on — the entire menu is eight noodle bowls and four toppings. ⚠ AND THE FREE CALL SYSTEM DOES NOT HELP EITHER, WHICH IS THE ONE THING WORTH KNOWING. Jiro's famous no-charge コール at the counter — ニンニク／ヤサイ／アブラ／カラメ, garlic, vegetables, back-fat, extra tare — reads like a way to customise around an ingredient, and it is not: ヤサイ is boiled beansprouts and cabbage piled on the same wheat noodles in the same bowl, and カラメ means MORE of the soy tare, i.e. more wheat. The calls change the mountain, never the base. ⚠ ONE VEGAN-ADJACENT TRAP ON THE TOPPING LIST: 生とじ卵 is a raw egg served with 魚粉, bonito powder — a fish product sitting in what looks like a plain egg topping.
